newsitem.title: UK: Eurotunnel up after bank agreement reached.
newsitem.headline: Eurotunnel up after bank agreement reached.

text.p: Shares in Anglo-French channel tunnel operator Eurotunnel Plc moved ahead on Thursday, after news its creditor banks agreed to a restructuring plan, dealers said.
Eurotunnel shares were up two pence, or 2.88 percent, to 71.5p by 0800 GMT, while the FTSE-100 index was 1.6 points, or 0.04 percent, higher at 4,389.3.
Eurotunnel said in a statement that a steering committee of banks had agreed a debt restructuring plan which would ensure the financial stability of the company for the six years.
The company said it was the board's view the plan was the "best possible compromise under present conditions".
Eurotunnel also said it aimed to achieve in 1997 an operating profit for the first time in its history.
The debt-laden firm posted a 1996 operating loss of 33 million stg, after depreciation and provisions compared with a year-earlier loss of 192 million stg.
After interest and other charges, the loss for the year was 685 million stg, an improvement of about 240 million versus 1995, the firm said.
